title: Fleet Orchestration Navigator — Scaling Slate, Throughput Timeline, and Immutable Change Log
creator: Aisha Kapoor
description: Design and deliver a new Fleet Orchestration Navigator in Console that combines (1) a compact 'Scaling Slate' for operator presets and per-fleet throttle curves, (2) a throughput timeline with anomaly overlays and per-model contribution breakdown, and (3) an immutable change log (versioned ledger) showing scaling/override actions, who made them, and rollback affordances. This is targeted at Dedicated customers and platform operators who need predictable throughput guarantees and rapid incident recovery. The feature must integrate with existing autoscaling policies, SLO alerting, and the telemetry pipeline.
acceptance_criteria: Scaling Slate provides preset manager + custom curve editor; presets can be saved per-operator and applied to fleets
Throughput timeline displays 48h/7d/30d views with per-model stacked contributions and latency P50/P95 overlays
Anomalies (throttles, capacity breaches, fallback events) are flagged and link to related incident notes
Immutable change log is append-only, shows actor, timestamp, before/after policy, and includes a 'revert to previous' workflow that opens a canary rollout
APIs emitted for any operator action to populate audit logs and trigger telemetry events (names documented below)
Feature gated behind console.feature.flags.fleet_navigator and rolled out with a 10% canary before 100% release
tasks: Finalize UX flows for Scaling Slate with Design
Frontend: implement timeline component and anomaly markers
Telemetry: add event names and attributes for operator actions
E2E: create smoke tests for applying presets and reverting changes
Docs: draft console guide and runbook for operator on-call
implementation_notes: Backend data model: scaling_presets table (id, fleet_id, name, payload_json, created_by, created_at)
History retention default 365 days; configurable per-org (consider legal/enterprise requests)
Performance: timeline queries must use pre-aggregated timeseries (rollups) to avoid heavy load on large fleets
Rollout: feature flag + canary (10% -> 25% -> 50% -> 100%), monitor on-apply error rate and API latency
design_feedback: Sofia Patel (Design): prefer compact preset chip UI; avoid long modal flows for common ops
Sofia Patel (Design): show primary metric (throughput tokens/s) and secondary (mean latency) in the slate header
Design review 2026-02-05: iterate on color palette for anomaly markers to maintain accessibility
engineering_feedback: Marco Ruiz (Backend): prefer storing preset payload as compressed JSONB to allow schema evolution
Yara Ibrahim (Frontend): timeline should be virtualized; large fleets can have thousands of model lines
Marco Ruiz (Backend): caution on retention: 90-day default recommended to control DB size; enterprise opt-in for 365
decisions: Use compressed JSONB for presets to allow flexible future fields
Default history retention set to 90 days to limit storage growth; enterprise override to 365 days
Expose a 'revert' workflow that creates a new override rather than mutating history (preserves immutability)
blockers: Need confirmation from Security on retention and export controls for audit logs
Telemetry pipeline requires a new attribute (operator_role) that infra must add before GA
